title: Customer signal-driven intake pipeline for hosted multi-interaction requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a signal-driven intake pipeline for Hosted API feature requests that span chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. The goal is to convert raw inbound customer asks into prioritized, handoff-ready work items using an automated decision graph and reviewer heuristics that encode SLA sensitivity, data sensitivity, technical complexity, and strategic fit. This should reduce time-to-triage for high-risk enterprise requests and improve gating consistency for Dedicated/Private eligibility.
acceptance_criteria: Automated intake classifier tags incoming requests with: SLA sensitivity, data sensitivity, required runtime capabilities (streaming/tool-calls/structured outputs), and estimated effort (T-shirt sizing).
Decision graph outputs a recommended lane (Self-serve, Enterprise Concierge, Security Review, Dedicated Eligibility, Blocker) and a priority score normalized across tenants.
PM/SE review flow surfaces top 10 enterprise requests per week with pre-populated context and recommended routing; reviewer can accept, override, or reassign within the UI.
End-to-end test with synthetic enterprise requests shows median triage time reduced by >=50% compared to baseline and no false-negative SLA-sensitive classifications across a 500-request sample.
Documentation (Confluence) and handoff checklist produced for SRE/Eng, including data collection schema and required logs for follow-up engineering analysis.
success_metrics: Median triage time (first actionable assignment) <= 48 hours for enterprise-flagged requests
Reduction in manual reviews for low-risk requests by 40%
Accuracy of SLA/data-sensitivity classifier >= 95% on labeled validation set
% of gated enterprise requests with clear routing decision >= 90%
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight orchestration layer that enriches inbound customer requests with signals from: request metadata, tenant profile (billing tier, committed SLA), chat/stream parsing heuristics (presence of streaming/tool call verbs), previous support tickets, and customer-provided security requirements. Use a declarative decision graph stored in Git (YAML) that maps signal combinations to lanes and actions. Surface this in the intake console with a two-stage human-in-the-loop review for high-impact routes.
tradeoffs: Automating more routing reduces manual effort but increases risk of incorrect gating for nuanced enterprise asks; keeping a human reviewer adds latency and headcount cost. We prioritize conservative routing for SLA/data-sensitive requests (favor human review) and more automated routing for high-volume, low-risk requests. Building the full ML classifier adds accuracy but increases engineering time; initial rollout will use deterministic rules + heuristics with rollout-to-ML in a later phase.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (4 weeks): deterministic decision graph + intake UI changes, enable on 25% of inbound web form requests and all inbound channel tagged enterprise requests. Phase 2 (8 weeks): add telemetry, metrics, and A/B test classifier; train ML model on labeled backlog. Phase 3 (12 weeks): full automation for low-risk lanes and enterprise concierge integration. Post-launch: quarterly review and decision-graph tuning.

2025-03-03: Engineering spike completed (ENG-27489) — validated ability to join tenant metadata with request payloads in the intake pipeline. Observed missing tenant SLA fields in ~12% of samples; added fallback heuristics.
2025-03-05: Security reviewed heuristics for data-sensitivity tagging; suggested adding explicit PII detection step for streaming examples. Marked as follow-up for Phase 2.
2025-03-07: Design reviewed intake UI mockups (DES-9803). Feedback: expose top 3 signals and recommended lane to reviewer; add quick override buttons for common actions.
2025-03-10: Synced with Solutions Eng on concierge workflow; agreed to pilot with three enterprise accounts. Updated acceptance criteria to include concierge handoff telemetry.
2025-03-10: Blockers: need product analytics quota for detailed triage metrics (request to infra team opened ENG-30211).
risks_mitigation: Risk: misclassification of SLA-sensitive requests. Mitigation: conservative default to human review if any high-sensitivity signal present; record all classifier decisions and build rapid rollback path. Risk: data privacy concerns when aggregating request text. Mitigation: store only hashed identifiers and short signal summaries; follow Security recommendations for PII detection.
